texts: My teacher told me I could not walk this way while still clutching my own importance, I had to put it down first before anything else.
doha: love asks for your head, are you willing to give it up
Love has room for only one; give up the self first, and only then may you enter.

They say the narrow way of devotion is only for those who are ready to lay down their heads first, keeping nothing back for themselves, so please write a doha about that complete surrender of the self for love.
laying down the head
At sunrise I place my own pride at the feet of the Beloved and walk on empty-handed under the sun, because love is the one bargain that asks for everything; write a doha about this self-sacrifice.
With the rising sun I lay my head at Your feet; take it, for love's price is the whole of me.
Every morning facing the sun I tell myself to let go of my ego and offer it up, and slowly it is getting easier to do.
head, feet, sun
doha with the sun about giving up your head and ego for the Beloved
the arrow and the head
An arrow of devotion has struck and I do not pull it out; I offer my head to the Beloved willingly, because only those who surrender everything can walk this path of love. Please write a doha for me.
The arrow struck and I did not flinch; I laid my head before the Beloved, for love asks for nothing less.
doha with an arrow, offering one's own head to the Beloved
My friend, struck by a sudden arrow of devotion, handed over his job, his plans, and his pride to his teacher without a second thought.
The washerman beat his clothes on the rocks and told me that love is like that: you must be beaten clean, and give up even your tongue and your pride, to be fit for the Beloved. Write me a doha.
The washerman beats the cloth, the Beloved beats the self; my tongue and my head are His, to cleanse as He will.
doha with a washerman and a tongue, giving up one's head for the Beloved
washerman, tongue, offering the head
The washerman near our lane says that to love someone truly you have to hold your tongue, take the beating and give up your head.
One thread holds me to my old self, and I hand it over too; love takes the head and gives back the Beloved.
I snapped the last thread tying me to my old life and walked off to follow my teacher, without bargaining for anything.
A single thread is all that I keep from the old life, and even that I will give; the path of love is for those who offer their heads to the Beloved without bargaining. Please compose a doha.
doha with a single thread, giving up the whole self for love
a thread and a head
love takes the head
My mother said I would never find real devotion until I stopped hedging every bet and gave something up with no hope of return.
short doha about how love takes everything, your head and your self
Love is no bargain; it takes the head and gives the Beloved, and the one who haggles never enters.
You cannot bargain with love; it wants your head, your pride, your cleverness, and everything else you have been holding on to, and only one who gives all may enter; please write a doha about it.
The swan sails into the sun and is lost in it; so I lay down my head and become nothing in the Beloved.
doha with a swan and the sun, offering one's head to love
swan into the sun, surrender
I watched a swan rise straight at the sun this morning and thought: that is how one should offer one's head to God, no looking back.
The sun climbs the sky and a swan glides into it, and I offer my head to the Beloved without hesitation, because love is only for those who lay down the self completely; compose a long doha for me.
My mother churned so hard her hands bled, and she said that is what you have to give up for something precious.
My mother turns the churn until her arms ache and says that love, too, is a churning in which you give your head and all your pride to get the butter of the Beloved, so write a doha.
The churn turns the cream and the Beloved turns the lover; the head is given, and only the butter remains.
doha with a churn, giving the head for the Beloved
the churn and the head
the price of love
Tell me a doha about the price of love, which is nothing less than your own head, set down willingly and with joy, with no hope of anything in return except the Beloved's smile.
Whoever would enter love must set his head down first and go in without it.
My friend says the only way to love someone fully is to stop protecting yourself and just give it all up with no guarantees.
doha: the price of love is your head, are you ready
The heron stands at the water's edge pretending to give up the world, but the true lover gives his head and gets nothing, not even praise; compose a doha about real sacrifice versus mere show.
A man at our ashram stands as still as a heron to look holy, while the quiet cook who gives everything is the one who loves.
The heron pretends at the water's edge; the true lover lays down his head in silence and asks no praise.
heron and the true offering
doha with a heron, true sacrifice of the head versus show
They say the lock on that old shrine opens only for those who have given up everything, and my grandmother went to try it.
No key will do; lay your head at the lock and the Beloved will open from within, if you give all.
The lock was never opened by any key, and love opens only to the one who lays his head on the threshold and waits; write a long doha about giving up the self so that the Beloved may open.
doha with a lock, opened only by giving up the head to love
lock opened by surrender
The palace and the stones are heaped around; love needs only the head, and the king must come with empty hands.
The prince left the palace and sat on a rough stone in the road, offering himself to his teacher with nothing else in his hands.
palace, stone, the head
The king sits in a palace and stones lie piled around it, but love does not take wealth or a crown; it asks for the head alone, so write me a doha about this complete offering of the self.
doha with a palace and a stone, giving the head to the Beloved
doha with a mirror and a cloud, offering one's self for love
mirror, cloud, offering the self
In the mirror I saw my own face and wished to offer it up, with the cloud passing over it; please write a doha about love that demands the head and the self, laid down gladly.
I looked in the mirror and offered up my face; a cloud passed and there was only the Beloved.
I looked in the mirror this morning and told the person there that it was time to give him up, as a cloud blew across the window.
pearl and water well, offering
Our village water well gives water only to those who bend low, and my grandfather said the same of love, with a pearl to show for it.
doha with a pearl and a water well, offering the head to love
The pearl-diver risks his head, the water well requires a bow; love asks both, and gives the Beloved.
A pearl is found only by the diver who risks his head and a water well is drawn only by one who bends, and love is much the same; compose a doha about giving oneself up wholly.
the cuckoo's whole song
A cuckoo sang in our garden all night with no thought of rest, and I felt that is how devotion should be, a total giving.
The cuckoo gives its whole song and keeps no note back; so must the lover give the head and keep nothing.
doha with a cuckoo giving its whole voice, like a lover giving his head
The cuckoo sings for the spring and gives its whole voice, holding nothing back, and so should the lover give his head to the Beloved; please compose a doha about total self-sacrifice in love.
The head is the entrance fee, and love lets in none who bring their heads along.
doha: to enter love you must give up your head
If you want this way, go forward and put down your head first, for love has no room for the one who keeps even a little back; write me a doha on this demand of total sacrifice.
give up the head
Someone at my retreat said that you cannot approach what you love while holding on to everything you own, even your own opinions.
Under the moon I set my head at His feet and let go of my own name, because love will only accept the one who offers everything; compose a long doha on that glad sacrifice.
By the light of the moon I laid down my head, and there was no more me to take it back.
doha with the moon, offering the head and self to the Beloved
the moon and the offering
One full moon night I decided to stop clinging to my name and my plans, and I felt lighter than I ever had before.
Not the clever, not the careful, but the one who sets down his head is accepted by the Beloved.
doha: only the one who gives up his head can truly love
not for the careful
My uncle always gave up first in every quarrel and I used to think he was weak, but now I think he was practicing a kind of love.
I know that love is not for the clever or the careful but for the one who lays his head down without a thought, and I want a doha that says it with a gentle and humble power.
doha: the cost of love is the self, keep nothing back
You cannot love and keep yourself; one of the two must be given, and the lover gives the self.
Please write a doha about the way true devotion costs you everything, and how it is no place for a person who wants to hold on to his pride, status or any bit of himself in the bargain.
When I first joined my teacher I thought I could keep everything, but he said gently that I'd have to put myself down at the start of love.
love costs the self
can you write a doha: you have to give up your head to taste love
Some say love is sweet, but they forget it first asks you to lay down your head and everything you own, then to remain smiling, so I want a long doha on the stern bargain at the root of love.
Love is sweet only after it has taken the head; and only the one who gave it knows the sweetness.
My mother warned me that real love will cost me something big, and I am just starting to see what she meant.
the first price
Gladly I lay down the head; what is a head, if it buys me the Beloved's one glance?
My friend gave up his comfortable career to follow his teacher and told me it didn't feel like losing anything at all.
doha about gladly sacrificing yourself for the beloved
Please compose a doha for a lover who is ready to sacrifice his very life and ego for the Beloved without reluctance, and who treats the offering as the greatest of joys rather than a loss.
joyful sacrifice
milk, lamp, the whole offering
Every dawn I fill the lamp and pour milk for the Lord, but my teacher says I should be offering my pride, not only these things.
doha with milk and a lamp, but the real offering is the head
Milk before the lamp is an offering small; the head laid before the Beloved is the offering that is whole.
I pour milk before the lamp each dawn and offer my head as a pledge, for love asks the whole being, not a part; write a doha about devotion where the lover gives up all he is.
I tried giving myself to a cause by halves and failed, then gave it everything and found the loss felt like gain.
doha: love doesn't accept half-measures, you give your head or nothing
all or nothing
There is no half-way in the path of love; it asks the head, the heart and all that you are, and so I want a doha on the lover who gives it all and stops counting his loss.
Half is no offering; give the whole head and the whole heart, or stand outside and watch the lovers pass.
the touchstone of sacrifice
My grandfather's love for his wife was tested on the touchstone of a famine, when he gave her his last bread and said nothing.
doha with a touchstone, love proven by sacrificing the head
A metal is tested on the touchstone and the lover is tested by whether he will give up his head, so please compose a doha for me about proving one's love through complete self-sacrifice.
The touchstone tests the metal, the Beloved tests the lover; whoever gives his head has passed.
doha: love takes only your head, not your gifts
Tell me in a doha how love will not take your money, your clever words or your good deeds as payment, but only the head itself, handed over in silence and willingness, with no thought of reward.
only the head will do
No payment is taken, no sermon heard; love accepts one offering only, and that is the head.
People tried to buy their way into my teacher's circle with gifts, but he turned them all away and asked what they were willing to lose.
My teacher says there is nothing fancy about it, you give yourself up completely and that is that, no tricks or bargains.
short doha: love is for those who give up their head
If you want to taste love you must give up your head, there is no other way; compose a gentle doha that says this plainly and without any ornament, for someone about to take that very step.
put down your head
Whoever would know this must first put down his head; there is no second way to the Beloved.
one-string lute, one head
The one-string lute needs a single string, and love needs a single offering, the head; please compose a long doha for the singer who lays down his whole self in order to sing the Beloved's name.
doha with a one-string lute, giving the head to the Beloved
A wandering singer with a one-string lute told me that you can sing of love only after you stop caring for your own life.
One-string lute, one song, one offering; the singer lays down his head and plays the Beloved's name.
The sword is raised and the lover bows; this is no loss to him, for love has asked and he has given.
sword and bowed head
doha with a sword, bowing the head in surrender to love
My grandfather said the real warrior is the one who lays down his sword and bows his head to the one he loves.
When the sword is raised, the lover bows his head gladly, knowing that love asks for nothing less than all; compose a doha on the beauty of such complete surrender in the path of love.
The washerman soaps and beats the cloth and returns it clean, and the Beloved does the same with the self, so give up your head and let Him wash you; compose a long doha on this.
The washerman by our lane says every cloth he cleans must first surrender to being beaten, and I thought that was true of the heart too.
The washerman beats the cloth to make it clean; the Beloved beats the self, and the head is the soap.
washerman, the self beaten clean
doha with a washerman, letting go of the self in love
Outside the mosque I paused and told myself that real prayer is to lay the head down, and not just on the ground, but in the heart, as an offering of pride; write a doha for this complete humbling.
mosque, head to the ground
The imam at our mosque said that bowing is easy but the head you really have to give up is the proud one inside.
doha with a mosque, offering the head in love, not just in prayer
At the mosque I bowed my head to the ground, but love asks for more: bow the self, and the Beloved will meet you.
At dawn there was dew on the grass and my shadow was long, and I decided to stop holding on to what I thought I was.
doha with dew and a shadow, giving up the self to love
With dew on the grass and a long shadow at my feet, I laid my head down, prepared to lose it all for the Beloved, because love is only for those who give up the self; compose a doha.
The dew is brief and the shadow long; I lay my head down and let both be taken for the Beloved's sake.
dew, shadow, offering the head
Two cannot enter here: either I do or the Beloved does; I laid my head down so He could.
a doha about love where only one can enter, the self must be dropped
When I joined the group, the elder told me you cannot bring your whole ego into this room, and I had to drop it at the entrance.
I have been told the way of love is so narrow that two cannot pass, and one of them must be the self, and it must be given up; please write me a doha on this self-giving for the Beloved.
only one fits
What the lover gives, he does not miss; he has put his head at the Beloved's feet and found it there.
giving without regret
Why should the lover regret what he gives up for love, when that is the very currency of the path? Please write a doha showing the head laid down, without grief, at the feet of the Beloved.
When my sister gave up her chances abroad to care for our mother she did it without a trace of regret, just a calm joy.
doha about giving up your head for love without regret
They put a mark on the forehead of the one who was about to give up everything, and he walked a thorny road smiling.
The forehead mark is on the brow and the thorn is in the foot; the lover walks on, his head already given.
forehead mark and thorn
A forehead mark is put on the head that will be given, and the thorn is borne with a smile, because love will take nothing less than the lover himself; compose a doha in this spirit.
doha with a forehead mark and a thorn, offering the head for love
He lays his head down and eats the bitter gourd as honey; love has made the bitterest taste sweet.
bitter gourd, offered head
A bitter gourd is fed to the one who has given up everything, and he eats it like honey, because he has laid down his head for the Beloved; write a doha on this strange sweetness.
doha with a bitter gourd for the lover who gave his head and tastes sweetness
My grandmother used to say that if you've really given yourself to something, even a bitter gourd tastes sweet, and I think she meant love.
By the water well I hung my pride on a hook and drew up pure water, for love asks the head to bend before it gives; compose a long doha about the self-sacrifice that precedes the gift of love.
I saw an old man bend very low to draw water from the water well, and I thought love asks the same, a head bowed.
bowing at the water well
doha with a water well, bowing the head in love
The water well gives only to the one who bends; the head bows low, and love is drawn up.
The swan leaves the lake behind and does not look back; the lover leaves his head and enters the Beloved.
A swan took off from the lake this morning leaving everything behind, and I felt that I should do the same with my ego.
The swan leaves the lake for the far hills with nothing and no regrets, and so should the lover leave his old self behind, head and all; write me a doha about total surrender in love.
swan leaves everything
doha with a swan leaving, giving up the self for love
doha with a lamp and a lotus, giving oneself to love
The lamp gives itself to the dark until it is gone, the lotus gives itself to the morning; so the lover to the Beloved.
I watched a lamp burn down beside the lotus pond and thought how lovely it is to give oneself entirely until nothing remains.
lamp and lotus, self-giving
Beside the lotus the lamp burns lower and lower till it is gone, and so the lover gives himself up to the Beloved, drop by drop and head and all; please write a long doha about it.
The musk deer seeks the scent he carries, the traveler leaves his road; the lover leaves his head.
musk deer and traveler, offering
A traveler and a musk deer crossed my path on the same day, one leaving all behind and the other chasing his own scent, and I felt shown something.
doha with a musk deer and a traveler, giving up the head in love
The musk deer dies of the scent he carries and the traveler walks on without looking back, and both teach the lover to give his head up to the Beloved without hesitation; compose a doha.
The spinning wheel stopped the evening my grandmother decided to offer everything to God, and even the rainbird outside went quiet.
spinning wheel, rainbird
doha with a spinning wheel and a rainbird, laying down the self for love
The spinning wheel stops, the rainbird stops calling, and the lover lays down his head in quiet, for love will accept nothing but the whole self; please write a doha about that surrender.
Spinning wheel and rainbird fall silent, and the lover lays down his head; love has taken the whole of him.
doha for those who think love is easy but it asks for your head
Write me a doha for those who think love is only sweet words and gentle smiles, and have never realised that it demands a full surrender of the self, head first, without any bargaining.
love is not cheap
Sweet words are only the beginning of love; its heart is entered by the one who leaves his head outside.
My teenage son thinks love is all flowers and texts, and I wish I could explain that it takes giving something real of yourself.
The peacock fans out his feathers and the moneylender counts his wealth, but the lover has nothing but his head to offer and offers it gladly; compose a doha about such humble, whole surrender.
The peacock shows his feathers, the moneylender counts his coins, the lover lays down his head and wins.
peacock, moneylender, the head
The moneylender's son showed off like a peacock at the fair, while the poor boy quietly gave his only blanket to a stranger, and I thought: there is love.
doha with a peacock and a moneylender, giving the head for love
To cross the bridge to the Beloved you must lay your head on the first plank and walk over without it; please compose a long doha about the self-sacrifice that love demands of every pilgrim.
My father crossed the old bridge to his village for the last time and gave up his claim to the land, saying it was easier to walk without it.
The bridge to the Beloved is narrow; the head is the toll, and the lover crosses lighter for having paid it.
doha with a bridge, giving the head as the price for crossing to love
crossing the bridge
doha with a forest and a cloud, the head given in love
forest and cloud, offering
In the forest under a heavy cloud I put down my pride and my name, because love will only enter an empty heart, and I want a doha about this joyous giving up of everything.
We walked into the forest under a heavy cloud and my teacher asked each of us to leave one thing behind, and I left my pride.
In the forest the cloud hangs low; I set down my head, and the Beloved passes through the empty place.
An old sandalwood was cut near our home yet still scented the axe man's hands, and it reminded me what love is like.
doha with sandalwood that perfumes the axe, giving the head in love

An old sandalwood was cut near our village yet still scented the axeman's hands, and love is like that, so please compose a doha on the uncomplaining sacrifice that gives its head to the one who asks.
sandalwood giving
Sandalwood perfumes the axe that fells it; the lover gives his head and blesses the one who takes it.
The philosopher's stone turns iron to treasure, but the lover turns himself into nothing by giving up his head, and so under a cloud I wrote this plea for a doha about utter surrender to love.
philosopher's stone and cloud
doha with a philosopher's stone and a cloud, giving the head to love
My teacher said that the philosopher's stone is nothing next to the person who can give himself up, and a cloud covered the sky as he spoke.
The philosopher's stone changes iron, the lover changes himself into nothing; the cloud shades the offered head.
A traveler stayed one night in our village with only a needle and a cloth, and in the morning he gave away even those and left smiling.
traveler gives needle and head
The traveler walks with a needle and nothing else, and offers even that to the Beloved, along with his head, and walks on unburdened; please write a long doha about complete renunciation for love.
doha with a traveler and a needle, offering the head for love
The traveler gave his needle and then his head; he needs nothing for a journey into the Beloved.
doha with sandalwood and a net, offering the head to the Beloved
Sandalwood to the axe, the bird to the net, the lover to the Beloved, each gives all it has.
sandalwood and net, giving
The net was thrown over the sandalwood grove and the old woodcutter laughed that even the wood gives itself to be caught, and I thought of love.
The sandalwood gives itself to the axe and the fowler's net catches the bird that did not mind losing its freedom, and so the lover offers his head; write a doha for me about this lovely loss.
peacock's total dance
The peacock danced in the courtyard like he had nothing to lose and I decided to give everything to my teacher just the same.
The peacock dances with his whole being, and the lover offers his whole head; both hold nothing back.
The peacock dances before the rain with his whole body and holds nothing back, and so the lover must give his head entirely; compose a doha for me with that spirit of total offering.
doha with a peacock dancing, giving up the head with joy
The tree gives fruit, shade and wood and asks nothing, and so the lover gives his head and all that he is to the Beloved, without counting the loss; write a long doha with that gentleness.
The tree gives its fruit, its shade and its wood; the lover gives his head, and calls it a fair trade.
the tree that gives
doha with a tree that gives everything, like a lover giving his head
The old tree behind our school gave shade to everyone and fruit to the birds and asked nothing, and my teacher said love is just like that.
